response.headline: Robot maker ABB shielded from tariffs in 'robust market'
response.summary: STORY: Swiss engineering company ABB said it is seeing strong customer demand.It's particularly from a surge in new data centres being built in the U.S. to process artificial intelligence.ABB makes factory robots, as well as motors and drives for factory production lines.On Thursday it also said it was seeing little impact on customers from U.S. import tariffs as it reported its third quarter results.ABB said its operating earnings before tax rose 12% to $1.74 billion.While new orders in the U.S. jumped 27% during the period.ABB generates around 7% of group revenues from data centres, up from 6% a year ago.It provides electrification products to keep server rooms online.Earlier this week ABB announced a partnership with chip maker Nvidia to develop the next generation of data centres.The company currently produces locally around 75-80% of the products it sells in the U.S. and is aiming to reach 90% by investing more in U.S. factories.

response.headline: TSMC profits blow past market forecast thanks to AI boom
response.summary: STORY: :: TSMCChip giant TSMC posted a record-breaking third-quarter profit Thursday, up 39.1%, smashing market expectations.But looming U.S. tariffs could cloud its outlook.Riding the AI boom, the company reported a net profit of nearly $15 billion, marking its sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth.:: FileDemand from major players like Apple and Nvidia continues to boost its bottom line.The Taiwan firm says AI demand is still strengthening, and is higher now than it had expected only three months ago. That follows similarly robust outlooks from other major tech players, including South Korea's Samsung and European chip gear leader ASML - a big supplier to TSMC. Despite the strong results, uncertainty looms.U.S. tariffs imposed by Donald Trump's administration weigh on the outlook.:: TSMCStill, TSMC is pushing ahead with a $100 billion U.S. expansion.That's on top of $65 billion already pledged for three plants in Arizona, one already operational.:: File TSMC shares are up 38% this year, outpacing Taiwan’s broader market as investors so far shrug off the tariff risks.
